source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Choose needle gauge by medication viscosity, route, site, and patient-specific factors","B":"Use the smallest-diameter needle available for every intramuscular medication regardless","C":"Choose gauge only from the client's stated pain tolerance rather than medication properties","D":"Use one default gauge for every injection because medication viscosity does not affect flow"}}
source_row.rationale: Needle gauge selection should consider the viscosity of the medication (thicker solutions may require a larger-diameter, lower-gauge-number needle to allow adequate flow), the injection route/site, and client-specific factors such as body size, to ensure both effective medication delivery and client comfort/safety.
source_row.source_detail: Needle selection depends on route, site, patient size and product characteristics; larger diameter corresponds to lower gauge number; current CDC administration guidance; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A nurse is selecting an appropriate needle gauge for an intramuscular injection of a viscous medication, and a colleague suggests just grabbing whatever gauge is fastest to reach for since gauge probably doesn't matter much.
